name: Kisspeptin restart

card.summary: An experimental peptide-based approach some use after testosterone or steroid use to try to restart the body's own hormone signalling, aimed at keeping muscle, skin and physique gains.
card.note: Kisspeptin is a research peptide; human studies have been short-term and not for recovery after steroid use.

quick.overview:
Kisspeptin restart refers to using kisspeptin, a hypothalamic peptide that drives the signal for the pituitary to release LH and FSH, as an experimental way to restart the hormone axis after suppression from testosterone or other androgens. The appearance link is the chain testosterone recovery, then retained muscle, body composition and skin or hair effects tied to androgen status.

Kisspeptin was discovered in 1996 as a melanoma metastasis suppressor and shown in 2003 to be essential for puberty. Clinical trials have given it briefly to healthy volunteers and patients with reproductive disorders and found it raises LH, but no trial has tested it as post-cycle therapy.
quick.how: Forum members describe it as an injected research peptide used in place of or alongside hCG, clomiphene or similar products, sometimes during ongoing TRT. Dose and sourcing details are not covered here.
quick.risks: It is not an approved drug. Reported human trials are short, and safety, purity of gray-market products and long-term effects on the axis are not established.

angle.text: Users describe it as a way to keep the pituitary-gonadal signal alive during or after androgen use so physique and related traits are maintained. The route from kisspeptin to those outcomes has not been tested in recovery studies.

lead: Kisspeptin restart, sometimes called kisspeptin PCT, is a community term for using kisspeptin peptides (commonly kisspeptin-10) to try to reactivate the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis after it has been suppressed by exogenous testosterone or anabolic steroids, or to keep it active during testosterone replacement.[1][2]

The appearance chain is indirect and, as users describe it, claimed: if the axis recovers or stays active, the person's own testosterone production and testicular function continue, which users hope will help them keep muscle, body composition, skin and hair traits tied to androgen status after finishing a cycle or in place of hCG while on TRT.[2][6][7]

Kisspeptins are encoded by the KISS1 gene and act on the GPR54 (Kiss1R) receptor on GnRH neurons, which triggers GnRH and then LH and FSH release. The gene was identified in 1996 as a metastasis suppressor in Danny Welch's laboratory in Hershey, Pennsylvania, and kisspeptin signalling was linked to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in 2003.[1] Kisspeptin is not an approved drug. Short-term human studies show it raises LH in healthy volunteers, and no published trial has tested it as a post-cycle recovery agent.[9][11][15]

The idea sits within a wider body of discussion about recovery after androgen use. Reviews describe testosterone recovery after stopping anabolic steroids as variable and often incomplete over months to years, with little controlled data on drugs used to speed it up.[16][17] Forum use of kisspeptin-10 is a self-directed attempt to fill that gap with a research peptide.

paras: In forum usage the term describes using an injectable kisspeptin product, most often kisspeptin-10, to stimulate the upstream signal for LH and FSH release. Users contrast it with hCG, which acts directly on the testes like LH, with gonadorelin (a GnRH analogue), and with oral clomiphene, which acts by blocking oestrogen feedback.[6][7][8] On TRT, exogenous testosterone suppresses the axis, so some users add an agent to keep testicular signalling going; after an androgen cycle, the goal is described as getting natural production back.
The practice is discussed as part of a wider recovery toolkit rather than a standalone protocol, and its mix of products varies between posters. Dosing and sourcing details are not described here.

Kisspeptin neurons in the hypothalamus act as a central regulator of the reproductive axis, integrating metabolic and steroid-feedback signals and gating GnRH release.[3][4] Energy balance and stress affect kisspeptin signalling, and a review links stress-related suppression of this system with functional hypothalamic amenorrhea in women.[5][3]

Wikipedia describes kisspeptin-54 (formerly metastin) as cleaved into shorter forms, including kisspeptin-13 and -14, that share a conserved C-terminal region and bind GPR54 on GnRH neurons.[1] A direct comparison in healthy men found kisspeptin-10 and kisspeptin-54 produced broadly similar gonadotrophin responses, with kisspeptin-54 raising plasma kisspeptin more because kisspeptin-10 has a much shorter half-life; GnRH was the more potent stimulator.[15]

Kisspeptin was identified in 1996 in Danny Welch's laboratory in Hershey, Pennsylvania, where the KiSS-1 gene, named after the town's chocolate, was found to suppress metastasis. The receptor was identified in rats in 1999 and the human version about two years later, and in 2003 independent groups linked receptor mutations to failure of puberty.[1]

Human administration studies followed from the mid-2000s, with Imperial College London groups led by Waljit Dhillo and Channa Jayasena among those reporting gonadotropin responses to kisspeptin-54 and kisspeptin-10 in healthy men and in patients.[15][19]

Wikipedia's anabolic steroid article says prolonged use suppresses the body's natural testosterone production through the HPG axis, in a dose-dependent way, with downstream effects including testicular atrophy and reduced sperm production, and that after a short course the axis usually recovers, with clomifene and hCG named as examples of agents used.[16]

A 2023 scoping review in Endocrine Connections of 36 studies found recovery of testosterone after stopping anabolic steroids to be variable and incomplete in many men, with some controlled studies finding values still lower than controls after a year or more, and noted few prospective controlled studies and no trials of post-cessation recovery drugs among those included.[17] A 2015 cross-sectional study of 24 long-term former users in Addiction found lower testosterone and testicular volume than non-using lifters and described withdrawal hypogonadism as common and frequently prolonged.[18]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and TRT communities
paras: On T Nation, kisspeptin-10 is described by some members as a possible substitute for hCG, with one poster saying it may offer similar value with no desensitisation over time.[6] Others say it keeps the testes active, though not optimally, rotate it with gonadorelin because they could not tolerate hCG, or mention it alongside clomiphene during a recovery attempt or alongside growth-hormone-releasing peptides when libido was low.[7][8][20][22]

These are self-reports with no controlled comparison, and posters differ on whether they combine it with ongoing testosterone. The topic is largely a bodybuilding and TRT forum subject; it has not been the subject of mainstream press features as a looksmaxxing practice.

Randomized and physiological trials in healthy people show kisspeptin administration raises gonadotropin levels, including a 2025 trial of intranasal kisspeptin and a 2025 trial finding it did not affect anxiety.[9][10] A 2013 study found a single kisspeptin-54 injection temporarily increased LH pulsatility in healthy women, and a 2022 trial examined bone metabolism in healthy men.[11][12]

A single-blinded crossover study of ten healthy men (Human Reproduction, 2015) gave three-hour infusions of kisspeptin-10, kisspeptin-54 and GnRH and found GnRH the most potent stimulator, with the two kisspeptins similar to each other.[15] A study of five healthy older men found LH and FSH responses to kisspeptin-54 at least preserved compared with young men, while testosterone rises were smaller.[19]

Registered trials have looked at hypothalamic amenorrhea, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and IVF.[13][14] Wikipedia notes a single infusion of kisspeptin-54 was tested for low libido and was well tolerated with some signal of effect in both sexes.[1] No study has examined recovery after steroid or testosterone use.

Kisspeptin has no approved uses. Published human studies are short-term infusions or injections in volunteers and patients, and long-term safety, repeated-use effects on the axis and the contents of gray-market research-peptide products have not been established by trials. Kisspeptin also has roles beyond reproduction: Wikipedia notes it can stimulate aldosterone and insulin release.[1]

Because the term refers to use after androgen suppression, the underlying risks of that suppression, including prolonged hypogonadism and associated mood and sexual symptoms, are documented separately.[17][18]

timeline.event: KiSS-1 identified as a metastasis suppressor in Danny Welch's lab in Hershey, Pennsylvania.[1]
The receptor GPR54 is identified in rats; the human receptor follows about two years later.[1]
Kisspeptin receptor mutations linked to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and failed puberty.[1]
Study shows a single kisspeptin-54 injection temporarily increases LH pulsatility in healthy women.[11]
Imperial College study compares IV kisspeptin-10, kisspeptin-54 and GnRH in ten healthy men; Addiction paper describes prolonged withdrawal hypogonadism in former steroid users.[15][18]
T Nation members discuss kisspeptin-10 as an hCG alternative on TRT.[6][7][8]
Scoping review of 36 studies finds testosterone recovery after steroid cessation variable and often incomplete; a forum thread reports kisspeptin-10 libido effects.[17][22]
Randomized trials report intranasal kisspeptin raising gonadotropins and no effect on anxiety.[9][10]

lore.intro: Kisspeptin appears on T Nation threads about TRT and recovery as an alternative or add-on to hCG, gonadorelin and clomiphene.[6][7][8]

claims.claim: Kisspeptin-10 can stand in for hCG to keep the testes active on TRT
claims.believers: Posters say it may provide similar value with less desensitisation and describe it as keeping testes active, though not optimal.[6][7]
claims.experts: Trials show kisspeptin raises LH in volunteers over short periods, but none has compared it with hCG on TRT.[9][11][15]

claims.claim: Kisspeptin can restart natural production after a steroid cycle
claims.believers: Members mention using it with clomiphene during recovery attempts.[8]
claims.experts: Reviews call recovery after steroid cessation variable and note no trials of recovery drugs; no study has tested kisspeptin for this.[17]

claims.claim: Working upstream of the pituitary is more physiological than hCG
claims.believers: Users who cannot tolerate hCG describe rotating kisspeptin-10 with gonadorelin.[20]
claims.experts: In healthy men GnRH was a more potent LH and FSH stimulus than either kisspeptin, and kisspeptin-10 has a much shorter half-life than kisspeptin-54.[15]

claims.claim: Kisspeptin helps low libido on TRT
claims.believers: A T Nation poster reports libido returning within weeks of adding kisspeptin-10 and growth-hormone-releasing peptides.[22]
claims.experts: A single kisspeptin-54 infusion was tested for low libido with signs of effect, per Wikipedia; repeated-use studies in TRT users have not been published.[1]

claims.claim: Kisspeptin keeps muscle and physique gains after a cycle
claims.believers: The reasoning is that restoring testosterone production prevents loss of gains.[2]
claims.experts: No study has linked kisspeptin use to retained lean mass after steroid use.[17]

claims.claim: The effect of kisspeptin on the axis is dose- and age-dependent
claims.believers: Forum users adjust protocols by feel and bloodwork.[8]
claims.experts: A small study found hypothalamic and pituitary responses preserved in older men, with smaller testosterone rises than in young men.[19]
